evidence.claim: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and installed a top governing body stacked with loyalists.
evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.excerpt: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and installed a top governing body stacked with loyalists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a high-salience party leadership outcome, contemporaneous and widely corroborated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as the incumbent who benefited from and shaped the leadership outcome.
contrary_evidence: This reports a party appointment process, not an open election.

evidence.claim: China was set to ease quarantine protocols and reduce mass testing after anger over the world's toughest curbs fueled widespread protests.
evidence.title: China set to loosen COVID curbs after week of historic protests
evidence.excerpt: China was set to ease quarantine protocols and reduce mass testing after anger over the world's toughest curbs fueled widespread protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a policy reversal tied to protest pressure; the causal link is reported through sources, not announced in a public rationale.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and immediately after the November 2022 protest wave.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution to Xi is indirect because the report describes a national policy shift rather than a quoted Xi directive.
contrary_evidence: This shows limited responsiveness, but it does not itself establish durable political freedom.

evidence.claim: The 20th CPC National Congress amended the Party Constitution to add a goal of gradually realizing common prosperity for all, a people-centered development philosophy, a domestic-economy-centered development pattern, and higher-quality, more equitable, sustainable, and secure development.
evidence.title: 20th CPC National Congress concludes in Beijing, Xi Jinping presides over closing session and delivers important speech
evidence.excerpt: The 20th CPC National Congress amended the Party Constitution to add a goal of gradually realizing common prosperity for all, a people-centered development philosophy, a domestic-economy-centered development pattern, and higher-quality, more equitable, sustainable, and secure development.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Also added to the Party Constitution are statements on gradually realizing the goal of common prosperity for all...'; congress closing-session summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official congress summary from the state news service directly records the adopted party-line language for 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers October 2022 and the ruler-period's core policy orientation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but indirect attribution: Xi presided over the congress and the language was adopted under his leadership, but it is a collective Party decision rather than a one-person order.
contrary_evidence: Policy language does not itself prove delivery or equitable outcomes.
The same congress also emphasizes Party control and state security, which can cut against welfare in practice.

evidence.claim: The 20th CPC National Congress report set explicit five-year objectives including high-quality development, a new pattern of development, greater science-and-technology self-reliance, more equitable basic public services, better social security, stronger living environments, and stronger national security.
evidence.title: CPC expounds on main objectives, tasks for next 5 years
evidence.excerpt: The 20th CPC National Congress report set explicit five-year objectives including high-quality development, a new pattern of development, greater science-and-technology self-reliance, more equitable basic public services, better social security, stronger living environments, and stronger national security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government transcript of Xi-led party program; precise and time-matched, but still official self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 program statement; exact fit for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High. Xi delivered the report personally and the listed objectives were the central program he was setting for the party-state.
contrary_evidence: This is official self-description, so it does not itself prove execution or success.

evidence.claim: The State Council issued a 33-measure package to stabilize the economy, including tax refunds, special bonds, social security premium deferrals, employment support, delayed loan repayment for affected borrowers, expanded inclusive lending, and more investment in infrastructure and consumption.
evidence.title: China issues policy package to stabilize economy
evidence.excerpt: The State Council issued a 33-measure package to stabilize the economy, including tax refunds, special bonds, social security premium deferrals, employment support, delayed loan repayment for affected borrowers, expanded inclusive lending, and more investment in infrastructure and consumption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy circular with concrete measures and implementation structure; strong evidence of operationalization, though official and not an outcome audit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tightly tied to the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium-high. The package was issued by the State Council under Xi's program; personal line-to-line implementation is indirect but centrally directed.
contrary_evidence: A policy package is not proof of effective delivery; later data show mixed macro outcomes and sectoral weakness.

evidence.claim: Banks directed more lending to small firms and manufacturing, credit to infrastructure increased, and regulators said they would improve services for new urban residents and ensure completion of houses under construction.
evidence.title: China's real economy sees stable credit growth in H1
evidence.excerpt: Banks directed more lending to small firms and manufacturing, credit to infrastructure increased, and regulators said they would improve services for new urban residents and ensure completion of houses under construction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official sector briefing with concrete allocation figures; useful for implementation, but still self-reported and not an independent audit.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 implementation data within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium. This shows party-state macro steering and credit allocation under Xi's broader program, but not a single-person causal chain.
contrary_evidence: Loan growth and targeted lending do not by themselves prove productive end-use or sustained impact.

evidence.claim: Xi called corruption a cancer to party vitality, said officials must not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to become corrupt, and demanded zero tolerance with no mercy for corruption.
evidence.title: Xi: Winning tough, protracted battle against corruption
evidence.excerpt: Xi called corruption a cancer to party vitality, said officials must not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to become corrupt, and demanded zero tolerance with no mercy for corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct speech by Xi at the 20th Congress; strong evidence of stated control priorities and discipline strategy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for intent and program ownership; lower for proving enforcement quality or impartiality.
contrary_evidence: The source is rhetorical unless paired with evidence on actual enforcement and selective application.

evidence.claim: The Organization Department said spot checks on officials' personal-matters reports rose from 3-5 percent annually to 10 percent annually, and all officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee were fully checked before the 20th Congress.
evidence.title: Press Center for 20th CPC National Congress
evidence.excerpt: The Organization Department said spot checks on officials' personal-matters reports rose from 3-5 percent annually to 10 percent annually, and all officials registered at and supervised by the CPC Central Committee were fully checked before the 20th Congress.
evidence.source_locator: press briefing snippet on personal-matters reporting and verification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official briefing text with concrete procedural changes; reliable for the existence of the measures, less so for effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Very close to the 2022 target year and the 20th Congress reshuffle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Medium-high. The measures are part of Xi's governance architecture, but the snippet does not isolate his personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The snippet proves monitoring rules, not that they were impartial or that hidden conflicts were actually eliminated.

evidence.claim: China issued 20 COVID response measures while still affirming the dynamic zero-COVID policy, saying the changes aimed to make responses more targeted and science-based and to minimize economic and social disruption.
evidence.title: China releases measures to optimize COVID-19 response
evidence.excerpt: China issued 20 COVID response measures while still affirming the dynamic zero-COVID policy, saying the changes aimed to make responses more targeted and science-based and to minimize economic and social disruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official policy notice with explicit implementation and adjustment language; strong for adaptation, not for outcome quality.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 policy shift within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High on program ownership, medium on operational execution because the source is a central mechanism rather than Xi's direct speech.
contrary_evidence: The source still defends the restrictive policy framework, so it is partial adaptation rather than full reversal.

evidence.claim: China announced it would downgrade COVID management to Class B from Jan. 8, citing vaccination, medicines, medical capacity, and accumulated experience, and said the shift was fact-based and would move focus from infection prevention to medical treatment.
evidence.title: China releases details of COVID-19 management shift
evidence.excerpt: China announced it would downgrade COVID management to Class B from Jan. 8, citing vaccination, medicines, medical capacity, and accumulated experience, and said the shift was fact-based and would move focus from infection prevention to medical treatment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with clear operational change and rationale; strong evidence of adaptation, though still official self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target period and immediately adjacent to year-end 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for policy direction, medium for execution because it reflects central collective adjustment after broad pressure and changing conditions.
contrary_evidence: This was reactive after severe disruption and public backlash, so it is better evidence of correction than of foresight.

unresolved_gaps: Direct command-and-control, custody, and launch-discipline evidence is still thin.
Concrete arms-control follow-through beyond declaratory no-first-use language is limited.
Crisis de-escalation evidence in the Taiwan and Russia-Ukraine settings is mostly indirect.
Direct evidence of Xi personally authorizing or restraining specific military moves is thin.
Civilian-protection and operational-conduct evidence during the Taiwan crisis is limited.
Evidence of actual mediation or de-escalation in Russia-Ukraine remains mostly declaratory.
Water, sanitation, and local service-variation evidence is thin compared with health, pensions, housing, and crisis response.
Chain-of-command evidence for specific repression episodes remains limited.
Independent evidence on courts, legislatures, and oversight bodies resisting capture is thin.
Succession and term-limit mechanics could be more directly documented as a de facto transfer-rule breach.
Independent evaluation of implementation quality across provinces and local-government debt stress remains limited.
Distributional evidence beyond averages and poverty-lifted subgroups could be stronger.
Water/sanitation and housing-quality evidence is thinner than health, pensions, and child-welfare evidence.
Independent evaluation of service quality, regional equity, and front-line delivery remains limited.
Direct, ruler-specific evidence on Xi's own assets, gifts, family business interests, or beneficial ownership is missing.
Independent findings on concealment or obstruction tied personally to Xi are absent.
Evidence of truthful correction versus rhetorical anti-corruption messaging is weak.
Independent evaluation of whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control is thin.
More subnational evidence on execution quality and correction would strengthen the adaptation story.
Durable causal impact of the COVID rollback and economic stabilization package remains under-audited.
